pin: Population-level behavioral proxies only. In-group is the time-varying top-N peer reviewers, not a psychological class and not the merge-key set. This file does not show that rejection sensitive dysphoria, negativity bias, or in-group preference caused any Bitcoin Core outcome.

identity_notes: Join table is analysis/user_identities/identity_mappings.json (7972 GitHub logins, 2526 IRC nicks). findings/data/enhanced_identity_resolution.json is a short manual alias list, not a per-login map, so it is not the join.
data_sources.review_volume: peer GitHub review objects only (not issue comments)

method_notes: In-group is time-varying: top-N by cumulative peer GitHub review objects with submitted_at < PR created_at. Self-reviews and bots are excluded. Ties break by identity string descending.
Before N distinct reviewers exist, group is unidentified and those PRs are left out of group comparisons, not dumped into out-group.
Headline windows are PRs created on or after 2016-01-01. Earlier review-object counts are an API hole.
Bootstrap is the percentile interval of the analysis unit (PR or contributor), 95%, independent resamples. It is not clustered on reviewer.

notes: Unit is the contributor. First peer response on their history. Included when that tone is neutral or negative. Outcome is another PR in the next 90 days. Censored when the log ends inside those 90 days. Group is in-group status on that PR, not a final label. Neutral is the common enriched label, so the negative-only row is the stricter cut.

If the in-group cell is empty, nobody was already in the top-N when their first peer response arrived. First responses sit earlier than reviewer-volume rank, so the in-group contrast is unidentified. The out-group figure is the newcomer return rate only.
Active at a horizon means some later PR is at or after that horizon. People whose first PR is too close to the dump end are not in that denominator.
became = entered the time-varying top-N after their first PR. left = never entered and no PR at or after 24 months, among people observable that long.
The outcome split is the group definition. Similar first-year treatment is the evidence. The survival gap between these two labels is not a separate finding.
Retrospective in-group membership was not knowable at entry. A fixed snapshot would have hidden that.

7_irc_silence_proxy.rule: Weak proxy. A concept-like IRC line (explicit idea phrasing, length >= 40) gets a negative or ambiguous reply in the same channel within 2 hours (nick mention, or one of the next 8 messages). The speaker then has no PR in the next 90 days and no IRC message after day 14 through day 90. Speech inside the first 14 days is allowed. Events still inside the log's last 90 days are censored. This is not observed preemptive withdrawal.

9_irc_presocialization.definition: Topic preface: in the 48 hours before created_at, the submitter's IRC identity posted in a bitcoin* channel and the line contained a title token (length >= 5, stopwords removed) or a bitcoin/bitcoin pull URL or the phrase 'pull request'. Presence is any such post, without the topic match. Unresolved authors (never seen in IRC) are not in the preface comparison.

stratification.note: Usable stratum: at least 30 finite observations on each side. Prior-PR bins are partly circular with later reviewer status.

quality.text: Out-group authors may submit different work. Lines changed, files touched, and prior PR count are partial proxies. A remaining gap is still not proof of hostility. Prior-PR strata are partly circular with who later reviews a lot.

merge_gap_persists_lines.reason: same sign and at least half the raw gap remains inside strata

sentiment_gap_persists_lines.reason: same sign and at least half the raw gap remains inside strata

circularity.text: Final top-N reviewers versus top-N PR authors. Overlap above 50% means the in-group/out-group cut is weaker than a newcomers-versus-regulars story: the same people are on both sides.

survival_bias.text: A fixed end-of-sample reviewer list would treat everyone who left as out-group and hide the dropout path. Metric 6 uses the time-varying set plus a retrospective 'later entered top-N' label. That label is not available at the first PR.

irc_nick_resolution.text: Match rate is the share of PR-author identities that appear at least once in the IRC log under the same unified id (or the same login string when the map has no IRC row). Below 60%, metrics 7 and 9 have elevated uncertainty.

active_social_filtering: sentiment gap persists after lines-changed strata
IRC topic-preface merge effect is negligible
passive_dropout: IRC silence proxy is higher outside the ever-in-group set (d <= -0.2)
structural_access_asymmetry: justification vocabulary |d| < 0.2 inside both preface strata

conditions_not_met_or_unknown: early treatment similarity not met (needs both |d| < 0.2)
sentiment gap does not shrink by half after lines strata
structural: preface does not account for most of the in/out merge gap under the stated rule
mechanism_disambiguation.reading: Scores count pre-specified conditions, not a model probability. A lead of 2 or more, with at least 2 conditions, is reported as the closer fingerprint. Otherwise the pattern is mixed or absent. Do not treat the label as a cause.

what_this_cannot_prove: We cannot observe psychological state. Nothing here is a diagnosis of rejection sensitive dysphoria, negativity bias, or any other trait in a person.
A population difference in merge rate, tone, attrition, or vocabulary is consistent with those mechanisms and does not require them.

Alternative explanations this design cannot rule out include a quality difference the proxies miss, topic selection, when the PR was opened, and structural access (who is already in the review channel).
The social-filtering reading needs both an asymmetric justification vocabulary and a sentiment gap that remains after the complexity and experience strata. Either one alone is not that reading.
Preemptive withdrawal is only the IRC-silence proxy defined in metric 7. This dataset cannot show who almost submitted a PR and did not.

CONFOUND FLAGS
Quality confound: flagged. Out-group authors may submit different work. Lines changed, files touched, and prior PR count are partial proxies. A remaining gap is still not proof of hostility. Prior-PR strata are partly circular with who later reviews a lot.
  lines strata, merge gap persists: True (same sign and at least half the raw gap remains inside strata)
  lines strata, sentiment gap persists: True (same sign and at least half the raw gap remains inside strata)
Circularity: overlap 15/20 = 75.0%. Flagged=True. Final top-N reviewers versus top-N PR authors. Overlap above 50% means the in-group/out-group cut is weaker than a newcomers-versus-regulars story: the same people are on both sides.
Survival bias: flagged as a design risk that metric 6 is there to show. A fixed end-of-sample reviewer list would treat everyone who left as out-group and hide the dropout path. Metric 6 uses the time-varying set plus a retrospective 'later entered top-N' label. That label is not available at the first PR.
IRC resolution: match rate 9.1% (236/2589). Flagged=True. Match rate is the share of PR-author identities that appear at least once in the IRC log under the same unified id (or the same login string when the map has no IRC row). Below 60%, metrics 7 and 9 have elevated uncertainty.

MECHANISM DISAMBIGUATION
Closer fingerprint: mixed
Condition counts: active_social_filtering=2, passive_dropout=1, structural_access_asymmetry=1
  met active_social_filtering: sentiment gap persists after lines-changed strata; IRC topic-preface merge effect is negligible
  met passive_dropout: IRC silence proxy is higher outside the ever-in-group set (d <= -0.2)
  met structural_access_asymmetry: justification vocabulary |d| < 0.2 inside both preface strata
  not met or unknown:
    - active: vocabulary |d| < 0.2
    - early treatment similarity not met (needs both |d| < 0.2)
    - sentiment gap does not shrink by half after lines strata
    - structural: preface does not account for most of the in/out merge gap under the stated rule
Scores count pre-specified conditions, not a model probability. A lead of 2 or more, with at least 2 conditions, is reported as the closer fingerprint. Otherwise the pattern is mixed or absent. Do not treat the label as a cause.

WHAT THIS CANNOT PROVE
1. We cannot observe psychological state. Nothing here is a diagnosis of rejection sensitive dysphoria, negativity bias, or any other trait in a person.
2. A population difference in merge rate, tone, attrition, or vocabulary is consistent with those mechanisms and does not require them.
3. Alternative explanations this design cannot rule out include a quality difference the proxies miss, topic selection, when the PR was opened, and structural access (who is already in the review channel).
4. The social-filtering reading needs both an asymmetric justification vocabulary and a sentiment gap that remains after the complexity and experience strata. Either one alone is not that reading.
5. Preemptive withdrawal is only the IRC-silence proxy defined in metric 7. This dataset cannot show who almost submitted a PR and did not.
